content:
The [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Audit any web page like Screaming Frog — title, headings, images, tags and a score. Enter your page URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Audit any public web page the way a site crawler does: fetch the page and check the title tag, meta description, heading structure, image alt text, canonical tag, robots meta and Open Graph tags, then score the page out of 100 with a list of what to fix. It is the Screaming Frog-style check for a single page — no crawl, no account, no install. The page is fetched from this site's server with strict safety limits (public addresses only, 10-second timeout, 2 MB cap), and nothing about the page is stored.

## How to use the Website SEO Audit

Start by typing or pasting your page URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the full URL of the page you want to audit, starting with https://.
2. Run the audit and wait a few seconds while the page is fetched and checked.
3. Read the score and work through the flagged items, worst first.

## How it works

The [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Auditing https://example.com reports a title of “Example Domain”, no meta description, one H1, and a score with the missing description flagged as the first fix. Try the same figures in the [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What the audit checks

Eight things: the title tag (present, and 30–60 characters), the meta description (present, and 70–160 characters), exactly one H1, heading levels in order with none skipped, alt text on every image, a canonical tag, the robots meta (flagging noindex), and Open Graph tags for sharing. Each check passes, warns or fails, and the score starts at 100 and loses 15 points per failure and 5 per warning.

## What it cannot see

The audit reads the page as it is served — it does not run JavaScript, log in, or follow links. Pages that render their content with JavaScript will look nearly empty to it, and anything behind a login cannot be fetched at all. For a full site crawl with every page, a desktop crawler such as Screaming Frog is still the right tool; this one answers “is this page's SEO in order?” in seconds.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Fix failures before warnings — a missing title costs more than a long one.
- Check your most important pages first: home, key services, top blog posts.
- Re-run the audit after fixing things to confirm the score moved.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an SEO audit?

A check of a web page against the basics search engines look for: a good title, a meta description, one H1, headings in order, alt text on images, a canonical tag and share tags. This tool checks all of them and scores the page out of 100. Try it with your own numbers in the [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I audit any website?

Any public page over http or https. Pages behind a login, and private or local addresses, cannot be fetched — the tool says so rather than guessing. Try it with your own numbers in the [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is the page I audit stored anywhere?

No. The page is fetched, checked and discarded. Nothing is saved, and the URL you enter is not logged with the result. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### Why is my score low if the page looks fine?

Usually a missing meta description or title, or several images without alt text. Work through the failed checks first — each one is worth 15 points. Try it with your own numbers in the [Website SEO Audit](/website-seo-audit) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
